Since the action of $\mathrm{Z}_k$ commutes with translations, we can assume  (renaming $\mathrm{c}+f$ as $\mathrm{c}$) that $d\cdot \mathrm{c}(v)=d' \cdot \mathrm{c}'(v)$ for every $v\neq 1^{k+1}$, and $\pi_{k-1}(d\cdot \mathrm{c}(1^{k+1}))=\pi_{k-1}(d' \cdot \mathrm{c}'(1^{k+1}))$. Hence there is $z\in \mathrm{Z}_k$ such that $(d\cdot \mathrm{c})(1^{k+1})=(d'\cdot \mathrm{c}')(1^{k+1})+z$. We claim that $z\in H_k$. Let us denote by $\mathrm{c}_z\in \mathrm{Z}_k^{\db{k+1}}$ the map that equals $z$ at  $1^{k+1}$ and 0 elsewhere. Then $\mathrm{c}+\mathrm{c}_z=d^{-1}d'\cdot \mathrm{c}'$, and we want to deduce that $z\in H_k$. nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 5.32
nodes.statement: By Lemma \ref{lem:cong-equi}, algebraically $\pi_H(\mathrm{X})$ is a $\mathrm{Z}_k/H_k$-bundle over $\pi_{k-1}(\pi_H(\mathrm{X}))$. By the paragraph below \eqref{diag:quots} we know that $\pi_{k-1}:\pi_H(\mathrm{X})\rightarrow \pi_{\eta_{k-1}(H)}(\mathrm{X}_{k-1})$ is an open continuous map. In order to prove that $\pi_H(\mathrm{X})$ is a principal $\mathrm{Z}_k/H_k$-bundle it suffices then to prove that the addition map $A_H:\pi_H(\mathrm{X})\times (\mathrm{Z}_k/H_k)\rightarrow \pi_H(\mathrm{X})$ defined as $(\pi_H(x),z+H_k)\mapsto \pi_H(x+z)$ is continuous. We have the following commutative diagram: \begin{equation} \begin{aligned}[c] \begin{tikzpicture} \matrix (m) [matrix of math nodes,row sep=3em,column sep=4em,minimum width=2em] {\mathrm{X}\times \mathrm{Z}_k & \mathrm{X} \\ \pi_H(\mathrm{X})\times \mathrm{Z}_k/H_k & \pi_H(\mathrm{X}), \\}; \path[-stealth] (m-1-1) edge node [above] {$A$} (m-1-2) (m-1-1) edge node [right] {$\pi_H\times \pi_{H_k}$} (m-2-1) (m-1-2) edge node [right] {$\pi_{H}$} (m-2-2) (m-2-1) edge node [above] {$A_{H}$} (m-2-2); \end{tikzpicture} \end{aligned} \end{equation} \vspace{-0.3cm} \noindent where $A:\mathrm{X}\times \mathrm{Z}_k\rightarrow \mathrm{X}$ is the addition action of $\mathrm{Z}_k$ on $\mathrm{X}$ and $\pi_{H_k}:\mathrm{Z}_k\rightarrow \mathrm{Z}_k/H_k$ is the quotient map. As $A$ and $\pi_H$ are continuous and $\pi_H\times \pi_{H_k}$ is open it follows that $A_H$ is continuous. It remains to check continuity of the difference map. As $\pi_H(\mathrm{X})$ is equipped with an \textsc{lch} topology by Proposition \ref{prop:quot-lcfr-nil}, let $(\pi_H(x_n),\pi_H(x_n')) \rightarrow (\pi_H(x),\pi_H(x'))$ for some elements $x_n,x_n',x,x'\in \mathrm{X}$ such that $(\pi_H(x_n),\pi_H(x_n')),(\pi_H(x),\pi_H(x'))$ are in the fiber-product $(\pi_H(\mathrm{X}))\times_{\mathrm{X}_{k-1}}(\pi_H(\mathrm{X}))$. By Lemma \ref{lem:conv-quot} we can assume without loss of generality that $x_n\rightarrow x$ and $x_n'\rightarrow x'$ in $\mathrm{X}$ as $n\rightarrow\infty$. Since $\pi_{k-1}(\pi_H(x_n)) = \pi_{k-1}(\pi_H(x'_n))$ there exists $z_n\in \mathrm{Z}_k$ such that $\pi_H(x_n) = \pi_H(x_n')+z_n+H_k= \pi_H(x_n'+z_n)$. Hence, for every $n\in \mathbb{N}$ there exists $\gamma_n\in H$ such that $\gamma_n(x_n)=x_n'+z_n$. In particular, applying $\pi_{k-1}$ on both sides of this equation we have $\eta_{k-1}(\gamma_n)(\pi_{k-1}(x_n)) = \pi_{k-1}(x_n')$. By Lemma \ref{lem:re-param-conv-seq} there exists $\gamma_n'\in H$ such that $\eta_{k-1}(\gamma_n)(\pi_{k-1}(x_n)) = \eta_{k-1}(\gamma_n')(\pi_{k-1}(x_n))$ and $\eta_{k-1}(\gamma_n')\rightarrow \eta_{k-1}(\gamma)$ for some $\gamma\in H$ as $n\rightarrow\infty$. By Lemma \ref{lem:conv-polish-group} we can assume without loss of generality that indeed $\gamma_n'\rightarrow \gamma$ in $\Theta(\mathrm{X})$ as $n\rightarrow\infty$. Hence, since now $\pi_{k-1}(\gamma_n(x_n)) = \pi_{k-1}(\gamma_n'(x_n))$, there exists $g_n\in \mathrm{Z}_k$ such that $\gamma_n(x_n) = \gamma_n'(x_n)+g_n$. By \eqref{eq:ft-fil} we have $g_n\in H_k$. Therefore $\gamma_n'(x_n)+g_n = \gamma_n(x_n)=x_n'+z_n$. This implies that $\gamma_n'(x_n)-x_n' = z_n-g_n$. By construction, and continuity of difference on $\mathrm{X}$, the left hand side of this equation converges (as $\gamma_n'\rightarrow \gamma$, $x_n\rightarrow x$ and $x_n'\rightarrow x'$). Hence $z_n-g_n\rightarrow \gamma(x)-x'$. Since $\pi_H(x_n)-\pi_H(x_n') = z_n+H_k = z_n-g_n+H_k$, we deduce that this converges to $(\gamma(x)-x')+H_k=\pi_H(x)-\pi_H(x')$.

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 5.33
nodes.statement: For $v\in \db{n}$ recall that $|v|:=v\sbr{1}+\cdots+v\sbr{n}$. It suffices to prove the result for any $S\subset \db{n}$ such that $|v|\le k$ for any $v\in S$. Indeed, if this case holds, then given a simplicial set $S'\subset \db{n}$, let $S^*:=\{v\in S:|v|\le k\}$, and note that if a sequence $(\pi_H\circ\hspace{-0.02 cm} \mathrm{c}_n)_n$ in $\hom({S'},\pi_H(\mathrm{X}))$ converges then $(\pi_H\circ\hspace{-0.02 cm}\mathrm{c}_n|_{S^*})_n$ in $\hom({S^*},\pi_H(\mathrm{X}))$ converges as well. Then by assumption there is a sequence $(\mathrm{c}_n')_n$ in $\hom({S^*},\mathrm{X})$ such that $\pi_H\circ\hspace{-0.02 cm}\mathrm{c}_n' = \pi_H\circ\hspace{-0.02 cm}\mathrm{c}_n|_{S^*}$ and such that $(\mathrm{c}_n')_n$ converges. It is then not hard to see that $\mathrm{c}_n'$ can be extended uniquely and continuously to an element of $\hom({S'},\mathrm{X})$ in such a way that these extensions also converge as $n\rightarrow\infty$. Abusing the notation let us consider now $\mathrm{c}_n'\in \hom({S'},\mathrm{X})$ such that $(\mathrm{c}_n')_n$ converges and $\pi_H\circ\hspace{-0.02 cm}\mathrm{c}_n'|_{S^*} = \pi_H\circ\hspace{-0.02 cm} \mathrm{c}_n|_{S^*}$. By uniqueness of completion we have $\pi_H\circ\hspace{-0.02 cm}\mathrm{c}_n' = \pi_H\circ\hspace{-0.02 cm} \mathrm{c}_n$, so the sequence $(\mathrm{c}_n')_n$ satisfies the desired conclusion. We have thus indeed reduced the task to proving that, given a $k$-step Lie-fibered nilspace $\mathrm{X}$, the proposition's conclusion holds for simplicial sets $S\subset \db{n}$ such that $|v|\le k$ for all $v\in S$. We prove this by induction on $k$. The case $k=0$ is trivial. For $k>0$, assuming the case $k-1$, let $\mathrm{c}_n\in \hom(S,\mathrm{X})$ be such that $\pi_H\circ\hspace{-0.02 cm}\mathrm{c}_n$ converges as $n\rightarrow\infty$. Then $\pi_{k-1}\circ\hspace{-0.02 cm}\pi_H\circ\hspace{-0.02 cm}\mathrm{c}_n = \pi_{\eta_{k-1}(H)}\circ\hspace{-0.02 cm} \pi_{k-1}\circ\hspace{-0.02 cm} \mathrm{c}_n$ is a convergent sequence in $\hom\big(S,\pi_{\eta_{k-1}(H)}(\mathrm{X}_{k-1})\big)$. By induction there exists $\pi_{k-1}\circ\hspace{-0.02 cm} \mathrm{c}_n'\in \hom(S,\mathrm{X}_{k-1})$ such that $(\pi_{k-1}\circ\hspace{-0.02 cm}\mathrm{c}_n')_n$ converges and $\pi_{\eta_{k-1}(H)} \circ\hspace{-0.02 cm} \pi_{k-1}\circ\hspace{-0.02 cm} \mathrm{c}_n' = \pi_{\eta_{k-1}(H)}\circ\hspace{-0.02 cm} \pi_{k-1}\circ\hspace{-0.02 cm} \mathrm{c}_n$. As $S$ does not contain elements $v$ with $|v|>k$, note that we can correct pointwise $\mathrm{c}_n'\in \hom(S,\mathrm{X})$ using Lemma \ref{lem:conv-quot} by adding an element $d_n\in \mathrm{Z}_k^S$ in such a way that the sequence $(\mathrm{c}_n'+d_n)_n$ still lies in $\hom(S,\mathrm{X})$ (this is because $\hom(S,\mathcal{D}_k(\mathrm{Z}_k))=\mathrm{Z}_k^S$, since $|v|\le k$ for all $v\in S$) but now converges as well. Thus, without loss of generality we can assume that $\mathrm{c}_n'$ itself converges in $\hom(S,\mathrm{X})$. The cube $\pi_H\circ\hspace{-0.02 cm}\mathrm{c}_n'$ is almost what we need. Indeed, we know that $\pi_H\circ\hspace{-0.02 cm}\mathrm{c}_n' = \pi_H\circ\hspace{-0.02 cm} \mathrm{c}_n+\overline{z_n}$ for some $\overline{z_n}\in (\mathrm{Z}_k/H_k)^{S}$. This follows from the fact that $\pi_H\circ\hspace{-0.02 cm}\mathrm{c}_n', \pi_H\circ\hspace{-0.02 cm} \mathrm{c}_n$ are equal modulo the factor map $\pi_{k-1}:\pi_H(\mathrm{X})\rightarrow \pi_{\eta_{k-1}(H)}(\mathrm{X}_{k-1})$. But then note that $\overline{z_n} = \pi_H\circ\hspace{-0.02 cm}\mathrm{c}_n'-\pi_H\circ\hspace{-0.02 cm} \mathrm{c}_n$ and both sequences $(\pi_H\circ\hspace{-0.02 cm} \mathrm{c}_n)_n$ and $(\pi_H\circ\hspace{-0.02 cm} \mathrm{c}_n')_n$ converge by hypothesis. Hence, by Lemma \ref{lem:cont-diff-map-coset} we have that $\overline{z_n}$ converges as well. By Lemma \ref{lem:conv-quot} there is a convergent sequence $(z_n)_n$ in $\mathrm{Z}_k^S$ such that $z_n+H_k^S = \overline{z_n}$ for every $n$. Then $\mathrm{c}_n'-z_n$ is in $\hom(S,\mathrm{X})$ (again using that $\hom(S,\mathcal{D}_k(\mathrm{Z}_k))=\mathrm{Z}_k^S$), converges, and satisfies $\pi_H\circ\hspace{-0.02 cm} (\mathrm{c}_n'-z_n)=\pi_H\circ\hspace{-0.02 cm} \mathrm{c}_n$, as required.

nodes.statement: For $v\in \db{n}$ recall that $|v|:=v\sbr{1}+\cdots+v\sbr{n}$. It suffices to prove the result for any $S\subset \db{n}$ such that $|v|\le k$ for any $v\in S$. nodes.section: 5.2 Topological aspects of groupable congruences and fiber-transitive filtrations

nodes.name: Extend the lifts
nodes.statement: Then by assumption there is a sequence $(\mathrm{c}_n')_n$ in $\hom({S^*},\mathrm{X})$ such that $\pi_H\circ\hspace{-0.02 cm}\mathrm{c}_n' = \pi_H\circ\hspace{-0.02 cm}\mathrm{c}_n|_{S^*}$ and such that $(\mathrm{c}_n')_n$ converges. It is then not hard to see that $\mathrm{c}_n'$ can be extended uniquely and continuously to an element of $\hom({S'},\mathrm{X})$ in such a way that these extensions also converge as $n\rightarrow\infty$. Abusing the notation let us consider now $\mathrm{c}_n'\in \hom({S'},\mathrm{X})$ such that $(\mathrm{c}_n')_n$ converges and $\pi_H\circ\hspace{-0.02 cm}\mathrm{c}_n'|_{S^*} = \pi_H\circ\hspace{-0.02 cm} \mathrm{c}_n|_{S^*}$. By uniqueness of completion we have  $\pi_H\circ\hspace{-0.02 cm}\mathrm{c}_n' = \pi_H\circ\hspace{-0.02 cm} \mathrm{c}_n$, so the sequence $(\mathrm{c}_n')_n$ satisfies the desired conclusion.
nodes.section: 5.2 Topological aspects of groupable congruences and fiber-transitive filtrations

nodes.name: Induction on $k$
nodes.statement: We have thus indeed reduced the task to proving that, given a $k$-step Lie-fibered nilspace $\mathrm{X}$, the proposition's conclusion holds for simplicial sets $S\subset \db{n}$ such that $|v|\le k$ for all $v\in S$. We prove this by induction on $k$. The case $k=0$ is trivial. For $k>0$, assuming the case $k-1$, let $\mathrm{c}_n\in \hom(S,\mathrm{X})$ be such that $\pi_H\circ\hspace{-0.02 cm}\mathrm{c}_n$ converges as $n\rightarrow\infty$. Then $\pi_{k-1}\circ\hspace{-0.02 cm}\pi_H\circ\hspace{-0.02 cm}\mathrm{c}_n = \pi_{\eta_{k-1}(H)}\circ\hspace{-0.02 cm} \pi_{k-1}\circ\hspace{-0.02 cm} \mathrm{c}_n$ is a convergent sequence in $\hom\big(S,\pi_{\eta_{k-1}(H)}(\mathrm{X}_{k-1})\big)$. By induction there exists $\pi_{k-1}\circ\hspace{-0.02 cm} \mathrm{c}_n'\in \hom(S,\mathrm{X}_{k-1})$ such that $(\pi_{k-1}\circ\hspace{-0.02 cm}\mathrm{c}_n')_n$ converges and $\pi_{\eta_{k-1}(H)} \circ\hspace{-0.02 cm} \pi_{k-1}\circ\hspace{-0.02 cm} \mathrm{c}_n' = \pi_{\eta_{k-1}(H)}\circ\hspace{-0.02 cm} \pi_{k-1}\circ\hspace{-0.02 cm} \mathrm{c}_n$. As $S$ does not contain elements $v$ with $|v|>k$, note that we can correct pointwise $\mathrm{c}_n'\in \hom(S,\mathrm{X})$ using Lemma \ref{lem:conv-quot} by adding an element $d_n\in \mathrm{Z}_k^S$ in such a way that the sequence $(\mathrm{c}_n'+d_n)_n$ still lies in $\hom(S,\mathrm{X})$ (this is because $\hom(S,\mathcal{D}_k(\mathrm{Z}_k))=\mathrm{Z}_k^S$, since $|v|\le k$ for all $v\in S$) but now converges as well. Thus, without loss of generality we can assume that $\mathrm{c}_n'$ itself converges in $\hom(S,\mathrm{X})$.

nodes.statement_short: Lift on the factor and correct pointwise.

nodes.name: Induction setup
nodes.statement: We have thus indeed reduced the task to proving that, given a $k$-step Lie-fibered nilspace $\mathrm{X}$, the proposition's conclusion holds for simplicial sets $S\subset \db{n}$ such that $|v|\le k$ for all $v\in S$. We prove this by induction on $k$. The case $k=0$ is trivial.

nodes.name: Lift via the factor
nodes.statement: For $k>0$, assuming the case $k-1$, let $\mathrm{c}_n\in \hom(S,\mathrm{X})$ be such that $\pi_H\circ\hspace{-0.02 cm}\mathrm{c}_n$ converges as $n\rightarrow\infty$. Then $\pi_{k-1}\circ\hspace{-0.02 cm}\pi_H\circ\hspace{-0.02 cm}\mathrm{c}_n = \pi_{\eta_{k-1}(H)}\circ\hspace{-0.02 cm} \pi_{k-1}\circ\hspace{-0.02 cm} \mathrm{c}_n$ is a convergent sequence in $\hom\big(S,\pi_{\eta_{k-1}(H)}(\mathrm{X}_{k-1})\big)$. By induction there exists $\pi_{k-1}\circ\hspace{-0.02 cm} \mathrm{c}_n'\in \hom(S,\mathrm{X}_{k-1})$ such that $(\pi_{k-1}\circ\hspace{-0.02 cm}\mathrm{c}_n')_n$ converges and $\pi_{\eta_{k-1}(H)} \circ\hspace{-0.02 cm} \pi_{k-1}\circ\hspace{-0.02 cm} \mathrm{c}_n' = \pi_{\eta_{k-1}(H)}\circ\hspace{-0.02 cm} \pi_{k-1}\circ\hspace{-0.02 cm} \mathrm{c}_n$. As $S$ does not contain elements $v$ with $|v|>k$, note that we can correct pointwise $\mathrm{c}_n'\in \hom(S,\mathrm{X})$ using Lemma \ref{lem:conv-quot} by adding an element $d_n\in \mathrm{Z}_k^S$ in such a way that the sequence $(\mathrm{c}_n'+d_n)_n$ still lies in $\hom(S,\mathrm{X})$ (this is because $\hom(S,\mathcal{D}_k(\mathrm{Z}_k))=\mathrm{Z}_k^S$, since $|v|\le k$ for all $v\in S$) but now converges as well. Thus, without loss of generality we can assume that $\mathrm{c}_n'$ itself converges in $\hom(S,\mathrm{X})$.
nodes.section: 5.2 Topological aspects of groupable congruences and fiber-transitive filtrations

nodes.name: Correct by convergent structure elements
nodes.statement: The cube $\pi_H\circ\hspace{-0.02 cm}\mathrm{c}_n'$ is almost what we need. Indeed, we know that $\pi_H\circ\hspace{-0.02 cm}\mathrm{c}_n' = \pi_H\circ\hspace{-0.02 cm} \mathrm{c}_n+\overline{z_n}$ for some $\overline{z_n}\in (\mathrm{Z}_k/H_k)^{S}$. This follows from the fact that $\pi_H\circ\hspace{-0.02 cm}\mathrm{c}_n', \pi_H\circ\hspace{-0.02 cm} \mathrm{c}_n$ are equal modulo the factor map $\pi_{k-1}:\pi_H(\mathrm{X})\rightarrow \pi_{\eta_{k-1}(H)}(\mathrm{X}_{k-1})$. But then note that $\overline{z_n} = \pi_H\circ\hspace{-0.02 cm}\mathrm{c}_n'-\pi_H\circ\hspace{-0.02 cm} \mathrm{c}_n$ and both sequences $(\pi_H\circ\hspace{-0.02 cm} \mathrm{c}_n)_n$ and $(\pi_H\circ\hspace{-0.02 cm} \mathrm{c}_n')_n$ converge by hypothesis. Hence, by Lemma \ref{lem:cont-diff-map-coset} we have that $\overline{z_n}$ converges as well. By Lemma \ref{lem:conv-quot} there is a convergent sequence $(z_n)_n$ in $\mathrm{Z}_k^S$ such that $z_n+H_k^S = \overline{z_n}$ for every $n$. Then $\mathrm{c}_n'-z_n$ is in $\hom(S,\mathrm{X})$ (again using that $\hom(S,\mathcal{D}_k(\mathrm{Z}_k))=\mathrm{Z}_k^S$), converges, and satisfies $\pi_H\circ\hspace{-0.02 cm} (\mathrm{c}_n'-z_n)=\pi_H\circ\hspace{-0.02 cm} \mathrm{c}_n$, as required.

nodes.name: Continuity of completion on quotients by closed fiber-transitive filtrations
nodes.statement: Let $\mathrm{X}$ be a $k$-step Lie-fibered nilspace and let $H_\bullet$ be a closed fiber-transitive filtration on $\mathrm{X}$. Then the completion function $\mathcal{K}:\mathrm{Cor}^{k+1}(\pi_H(\mathrm{X}))\rightarrow \pi_H(\mathrm{X})$ is continuous.
nodes.section: 5.2 Topological aspects of groupable congruences and fiber-transitive filtrations
assumptions: Let $\mathrm{X}$ be a $k$-step Lie-fibered nilspace and let $H_\bullet$ be a closed fiber-transitive filtration on $\mathrm{X}$.
conclusions: Then the completion function $\mathcal{K}:\mathrm{Cor}^{k+1}(\pi_H(\mathrm{X}))\rightarrow \pi_H(\mathrm{X})$ is continuous.
nodes.label: prop:cont-completion-coset

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 5.34
nodes.statement: Let $\pi_H\circ\hspace{-0.02 cm}\mathrm{c}_n'$ be a convergent sequence in $\mathrm{Cor}^{k+1}(\pi_H(\mathrm{X}))$. By Proposition \ref{prop:lift-of-simplicial} we can assume that $\mathrm{c}_n'\in \mathrm{Cor}^{k+1}(\mathrm{X})$ and converges to $\mathrm{c}'\in \mathrm{Cor}^{k+1}(\mathrm{X})$. For each $n\in \mathbb{N}$ let $\mathrm{c}_n\in \mathrm{C}^{k+1}(\mathrm{X})$ be the unique completion of $\mathrm{c}_n'$. Then by continuity of completion on $\mathrm{X}$, the cubes $\mathrm{c}_n$ converge to the cube $\mathrm{c}\in\mathrm{C}^{k+1}(\mathrm{X})$ which completes $\mathrm{c}'$. But then $\mathcal{K}(\pi_H\circ\hspace{-0.02 cm}\mathrm{c}_n')=\pi_H(\mathrm{c}_n(1^{k+1}))$, which converges (by continuity of $\pi_H$) to $\pi_H(\mathrm{c}(1^{k+1}))=\mathcal{K}(\pi_H\circ\hspace{-0.02 cm} \mathrm{c}')$.

nodes.name: Quotients of Lie-fibered nilspaces by closed fiber-transitive filtrations are Lie-fibered

nodes.section: 5.2 Topological aspects of groupable congruences and fiber-transitive filtrations
assumptions: Let $\mathrm{X}$ be a $k$-step Lie-fibered nilspace, and let $H_\bullet$ be a closed fiber-transitive filtration on $\mathrm{X}$.
conclusions: Then $\pi_H(\mathrm{X})$ equipped with the quotient topology is a $k$-step  Lie-fibered nilspace.
nodes.label: thm:coset-quot-closed

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 5.35
nodes.statement: Since $\sim_H$ is a groupable congruence, the algebraic part (i.e.\ that $\pi_H(\mathrm{X})$ is a $k$-step nilspace) follows from Lemma \ref{lem:gpequivcong} (as used in Lemma \ref{lem:cong-equi}). The topology on $\pi_H(\mathrm{X})$ is \textsc{lch} by Proposition \ref{prop:quot-lcfr-nil}. Now we want to check that the hypotheses of Lemma \ref{lem:eq-def-lch-nil} are satisfied. The cube sets on $\pi_H(\mathrm{X})$ are closed, by Proposition \ref{prop:closure-cubes-coset}. The continuity of the completion of $(k+1)$-corners in $\pi_H(\mathrm{X})$ follows from Proposition \ref{prop:cont-completion-coset}. As explained in Remark \ref{rem:comdiag}, this implies that $\mathcal{K}_{n+1}$ is continuous on $\pi_{\eta_n(H)}(\mathrm{X}_n)$. This shows that $\pi_H(\mathrm{X})$ is an \textsc{lch} $k$-step nilspace. Finally, we need to prove that the structure groups of $\pi_H(\mathrm{X})$ are Lie groups. Let us prove that $\mathrm{Z}_k(\pi_H(\mathrm{X})) \cong \mathrm{Z}_k(\mathrm{X})/H_k$ (as topological groups) and note that for any $i\in[k]$ the proof of $\mathrm{Z}_i(\pi_{\eta_i(H)}(\mathrm{X}_i)) \cong \mathrm{Z}_i(\mathrm{X})/\eta_i(H_i)$ follows similarly. The map $\pi_H:\mathrm{X}\rightarrow \pi_H(\mathrm{X})$ is a continuous and open fibration. Restricting to a fiber\footnote{Recall from Proposition \ref{prop:k-th-group-action} the definition of the $k$-th structure group of a $k$-step \textsc{lch} nilspace.} of $\pi_{k-1}$, we deduce that the $k$-th structure morphism $\phi_k:\mathrm{Z}_k(\mathrm{X})\rightarrow \mathrm{Z}_k(\pi_H(\mathrm{X}))$ is a continuous surjective homomorphism. The kernel of this map is precisely $H_k$. Indeed, for any $z\in \mathrm{Z}_k(\mathrm{X})$ we have $\phi_k(z)=0$ if and only if for any fixed $e\in \mathrm{X}$ we have that $\pi_H(e+z)=\pi_H(e)$. Then, by \eqref{eq:ft-fil} we have that $z\in H_k$. By the Open mapping theorem for Polish groups we have that $\mathrm{Z}_k(\mathrm{X})/H_k \cong \mathrm{Z}_k(\pi_H(\mathrm{X}))$ as topological groups. But now both $\mathrm{Z}_k(\mathrm{X})$ and $H_k$ are Lie groups (the first by hypothesis and the second because by Cartan's theorem it is a closed subgroup of a Lie group). Thus $\mathrm{Z}_k(\pi_H(\mathrm{X}))$ is a Lie group.

nodes.name: Fiber-discrete and fiber-cocompact groups on Lie-fibered nilspaces
nodes.statement: Let $\mathrm{X}$ be a $k$-step Lie-fibered nilspace and let $\Gamma$ be a fiber-transitive group on $\mathrm{X}$. We say that $\Gamma$ is \emph{fiber-discrete} if for every $j\in[k]$, the group $\eta_j(\Gamma)\cap \Theta_j(\mathrm{X}_j)$ is a discrete subgroup of $\Theta_j(\mathrm{X}_j)$. We say that $\Gamma$ is \emph{fiber-cocompact} if for every $j\in[k]$, the group $\eta_j(\Gamma)\cap \Theta_j(\mathrm{X}_j)$ is cocompact in $\Theta_j(\mathrm{X}_j)$.

nodes.name: Proof of Corollary 5.37
nodes.statement: By Theorem \ref{thm:coset-quot-closed} we have that $\pi_H(\mathrm{X})$ is a $k$-step Lie-fibered nilspace. To prove that $\pi_H(\mathrm{X})$ is a compact nilspace, by \cite[Definition 1.0.2]{Cand:Notes2} it suffices to prove that the topology on $\pi_H(\mathrm{X})$ is compact (we already know that $\mathrm{C}^n(\pi_H(\mathrm{X}))$ is closed for each $n$, by Theorem \ref{thm:coset-quot-closed}). We argue by induction on $k$, with the case $k=0$ being trivial. Assuming the case $k-1$, by \cite[Theorem 3.3]{Gleason} we have that $\mathrm{X}$ is a $Z_k/H_k$-bundle over $\mathrm{X}_{k-1}$ where $Z_k/H_k$ is a compact abelian Lie group. Thus for every $\pi_{k-1}(x)\in \mathrm{X}_{k-1}$ there exists an open set $U\subset \mathrm{X}_{k-1} $ such that $\pi_{k-1}^{-1}(U)$ is homeomorphic to $U\times Z_k/H_k$. For every $\pi_{k-1}(x)$ let $U_{\pi_{k-1}(x)}$ be such an open set. By compactness of $\mathrm{X}_{k-1}$ there is a finite cover $(U_{\pi_{k-1}(x_j)})_{j=1}^b$. Then, given any open covering $\cup_{i\in I} V_i$ of $\mathrm{X}$, by taking intersections we can assume that each $V_i$ is included in one of the open sets $\pi_{k-1}^{-1}(U_{\pi_{k-1}(x_j)})$. By Lebesgue's number lemma, there exists $\delta>0$ such that if a subset $C\subset \mathrm{X}_{k-1}$ has diameter $\mathrm{diam}(C)<\delta$, then $C$ is included in $U_{\pi_{k-1}(x_j)}$ for some $j\in [b]$. By compactness of $\mathrm{X}_{k-1}$, there exists a finite covering of $\mathrm{X}_{k-1}$ by balls of the form $B(\pi_{k-1}(x'_s),\delta/2)$, $s\in [m]$, for some $m\in \mathbb{N}$. The closed (hence compact) balls $\overline{B(\pi_{k-1}(x'_s),\delta/2)}$ clearly cover $\mathrm{X}_{k-1}$, and each of these compact sets is included in some $U_{\pi_{k-1}(x_{j_s})}$ for some $j_s\in[b]$. Thus, for each $s\in[m]$, since $\overline{B(\pi_{k-1}(x'_s),\delta/2)}\times (\mathrm{Z}_k/H_k)\subset U_{\pi_{k-1}(x_{j_s})}\times (\mathrm{Z}_k/H_k)$ and $U_{\pi_{k-1}(x_{j_s})}\times (\mathrm{Z}_k/H_k)$ is homeomorphic to $\pi_{k-1}^{-1}(U_{\pi_{k-1}(x_{j_s})})$, we have that $\cup_{i\in I} [V_i\cap \pi_{k-1}^{-1}(U_{\pi_{k-1}(x_{j_s})})]$ is an open covering of the compact set $\overline{B(\pi_{k-1}(x'_s),\delta/2)}\times (\mathrm{Z}_k/H_k)$. Thus, we can find a finite sub-cover, with corresponding finite index set $I_s\subset I$. Repeating this for every $s\in [m]$ and collecting, we deduce that $\cup_{s\in[m]}\cup_{i\in I_s} V_i$ is a finite sub-cover of $\cup_{i\in I} V_i$.

nodes.statement_short: Gleason gives a bundle with compact fiber.

nodes.name: Finite subcover
nodes.statement: By Lebesgue's number lemma, there exists $\delta>0$ such that if a subset $C\subset \mathrm{X}_{k-1}$ has diameter $\mathrm{diam}(C)<\delta$, then $C$ is included in $U_{\pi_{k-1}(x_j)}$ for some $j\in [b]$. By compactness of $\mathrm{X}_{k-1}$, there exists a finite covering of $\mathrm{X}_{k-1}$ by balls of the form $B(\pi_{k-1}(x'_s),\delta/2)$, $s\in [m]$, for some $m\in \mathbb{N}$. The closed (hence compact)  balls $\overline{B(\pi_{k-1}(x'_s),\delta/2)}$ clearly cover $\mathrm{X}_{k-1}$, and each of these compact sets is included in some $U_{\pi_{k-1}(x_{j_s})}$ for some $j_s\in[b]$. Thus, for each $s\in[m]$, since $\overline{B(\pi_{k-1}(x'_s),\delta/2)}\times (\mathrm{Z}_k/H_k)\subset U_{\pi_{k-1}(x_{j_s})}\times (\mathrm{Z}_k/H_k)$ and $U_{\pi_{k-1}(x_{j_s})}\times (\mathrm{Z}_k/H_k)$ is homeomorphic to $\pi_{k-1}^{-1}(U_{\pi_{k-1}(x_{j_s})})$, we have that $\cup_{i\in I} [V_i\cap \pi_{k-1}^{-1}(U_{\pi_{k-1}(x_{j_s})})]$ is an open covering of the compact set $\overline{B(\pi_{k-1}(x'_s),\delta/2)}\times (\mathrm{Z}_k/H_k)$. Thus, we can find a finite sub-cover, with corresponding finite index set $I_s\subset I$. Repeating this for every $s\in [m]$ and collecting, we deduce that $\cup_{s\in[m]}\cup_{i\in I_s} V_i$ is a finite sub-cover of $\cup_{i\in I} V_i$.
nodes.section: 5.2 Topological aspects of groupable congruences and fiber-transitive filtrations

nodes.name: Fiber-cocompact but not cocompact
nodes.statement: Given a nilspace $\mathrm{X}$ and a closed fiber-transitive group $H\leq \Theta(\mathrm{X})$ that is also fiber-cocompact, in general $H$ need not be a cocompact subgroup of $\Theta(\mathrm{X})$. For example, let $F=\mathcal{D}_1(\mathbb{R})\times \mathcal{D}_2(\mathbb{R})$ and consider $H=\langle \alpha,\beta \rangle$ where $\alpha(x,y)=(x+1,y)$ and $\beta(x,y)=(x,y+1)$. This group $H$ is straightforwardly checked to be fiber-cocompact in $\Theta(F)$. On the other hand we have $\Theta(F)=\{(x,y)\mapsto(x+a,y+b+cx):a,b,c\in \mathbb{R}\}$. Note that this group is isomorphic to the Heisenberg group $\mathcal{H}= \begin{psmallmatrix} 1 & \mathbb{R} & \mathbb{R}\\[0.1em]0 & 1 & \mathbb{R}\\[0.1em] 0 & 0 & 1 \end{psmallmatrix}$. Letting $\gamma_{a,b,c}\in \Theta(F)$ be the map $(x,y)\mapsto (x+a,y+b+cx)$, it is straightforwardly checked that the map $\varphi:\Theta(F)\rightarrow \mathcal{H}$, $\gamma_{a,b,c}\mapsto \begin{psmallmatrix} 1 & c & b\\[0.1em]0 & 1 & a\\[0.1em] 0 & 0 & 1 \end{psmallmatrix}$ is a group isomorphism. Thus, in order to show that $H\subset \Theta(F)$ is not co-compact, it suffices to check that $\varphi(H)\subset \mathcal{H}$ is not co-compact. A simple calculation shows that $\varphi(H)=\langle \varphi(\alpha),\varphi(\beta) \rangle=\begin{psmallmatrix} 1 & 0 & \mathbb{Z}\\[0.1em]0 & 1 & \mathbb{Z}\\[0.1em] 0 & 0 & 1 \end{psmallmatrix}$ is a subgroup of $R:= \begin{psmallmatrix} 1 & 0 & \mathbb{R}\\[0.1em]0 & 1 & \mathbb{R}\\[0.1em] 0 & 0 & 1 \end{psmallmatrix}$. Thus, if $\varphi(H)$ is co-compact then $R$ should also be co-compact. But $R$ is a normal subgroup of $\mathcal{H}$ and a direct computation shows that $\mathcal{H}/R\cong \mathbb{R}$. Hence $\varphi(H)$ cannot be co-compact.
nodes.section: 5.2 Topological aspects of groupable congruences and fiber-transitive filtrations
nodes.statement_short: $\langle(x+1,y),(x,y+1)\rangle$ on $\mathcal{D}_1(\mathbb{R})\times\mathcal{D}_2(\mathbb{R})$ is fiber-cocompact but not cocompact in the Heisenberg group $\Theta(F)$.
nodes.label: ex:fiber-co-comp-not-co-comp

nodes.name: Necessary and sufficient closure condition for free nilspaces
nodes.statement: One may naturally wonder to what extent the closure property in Definition \ref{def:oldclosed} is \emph{necessary} to ensure that the quotient of $\mathrm{X}$ by $\sim_H$ is a Lie-fibered nilspace. It turns out that for $\mathrm{X}$ a \emph{free} nilspace, a variant condition can be proved to be necessary and sufficient. More precisely, if $F$ is a $k$-step free nilspace and $H$ is a fiber-transitive group on $F$, it can be proved that $\pi_H(F)$ is a Lie-fibered nilspace if and only if for every $i\in [k]$ the group $\eta_i(\compl{H})$ is a closed subgroup of $\Theta(F_i)$. We shall not need this fact in this paper, so let us just outline the argument here. First one proves that more generally if $H$ is a fiber-transitive group on a Lie-fibered nilspace, then $\compl{H}=\ker(\widehat{\pi_H})$ and so $\compl{H}$ must be a closed subgroup of $\Theta(F)$. Then, the same fact applied on $F_i$ implies that $\compl{\eta_i(H)}$ is closed in $\Theta(F_i)$. This yields the necessity of the above condition. Then, using that $F$ is a free nilspace, the additional property that for every $i\in [k]$ we obtain the additional fact that $\eta_i(\compl{H})=\compl{\eta_i(H)}$, and this implies the sufficiency of the above condition (indeed we then need not ask for all the terms in the filtration of ${\compl{H}}$ to be closed, because the filtration is $({\compl{H}}\cap \Theta_i(F))_{i\in[k]}$, and similarly for lower steps. Hence, as $\Theta_i(F)$ is always closed, it suffices to require ${\compl{H}}$ to be closed, and for lower-step factors it suffices to require $\eta_i(\compl{H})$ to be closed).
nodes.section: 5.2 Topological aspects of groupable congruences and fiber-transitive filtrations

nodes.name: Free groupable congruence
nodes.statement: Let $\mathrm{X}$ be a $k$-step nilspace. We say that a groupable congruence $\sim$ on $\mathrm{X}$ is \emph{free} if there exists a subfiltration $H_\bullet$ of $\Theta(\mathrm{X})^{(\sim)}_\bullet$ such that $H_\bullet$ is a closed fiber-transitive filtration on $\mathrm{X}$ with $\sim=\sim_H$ and such that the action of $H$ on $\mathrm{X}$ is \emph{free}. That is, for every $x,y\in \mathrm{X}$ with $x\sim y$ there is a unique element $g\in H$ such that $gx=y$. We also say that that the filtration $H_\bullet$ is \emph{free fiber-transitive} on $\mathrm{X}$.
nodes.section: 5.3 Free groupable congruences and embeddings
nodes.label: def:free-group-cong

nodes.name: Different filtrations realizing the same congruence
nodes.statement: Note that for $\sim$ to be free we indeed require just \emph{some} fiber-transitive filtration realizing $\sim$ to be free. Indeed, there can be more than one fiber-transitive filtration yielding the same quotient nilspace. For example, let $F=\mathcal{D}_1(\mathbb{Z})\times \mathcal{D}_2(\mathbb{Z})$ and let $\alpha(x,y):=(x+2,y)$, $\beta(x,y)=(x,y+2)$ and $\gamma(x,y):=(x,y+2x)$. It is easy to see that $H:=\langle \alpha,\beta\rangle$ and $H':=\langle \alpha,\beta,\gamma\rangle$ generate the same congruence and so $\pi_H(F) \cong \pi_{H'}(F)$ (putting on both $H$ and $H'$ the filtration induced by $\Theta_\bullet (F)$). However $H_\bullet$ acts freely, whereas $H'_\bullet$ does not.
nodes.section: 5.3 Free groupable congruences and embeddings
nodes.label: rem:different-filtr

nodes.name: Fibers of free groupable congruences are principal homogeneous spaces
nodes.statement: Recall from \eqref{eq:ft-fil} that if $\sim$ is a groupable congruence on $\mathrm{X}$ then, letting $G_\bullet$ be the corresponding filtration on $\big(\Theta(\mathrm{X})^{(\sim)}\cap \Theta_i(\mathrm{X})\big)_{i\geq 0}$, the action of $G_i$ on each intersection of a $\sim$-fiber and a $\pi_{i-1}$-fiber is transitive. Hence, if $\sim$ is also free (i.e.\ $G_\bullet$ is free fiber-transitive), then each intersection of a $\sim$-fiber and a $\pi_{i-1}$-fiber is a \emph{principal homogeneous space} of $G_i$.
nodes.section: 5.3 Free groupable congruences and embeddings

nodes.name: Free fiber-transitivity descends to factors
nodes.statement: If $H_\bullet$ is a free fiber-transitive filtration on $\mathrm{X}$, then for each $i\in[k]$ the filtration $\eta_j(H_\bullet)$ is free fiber-transitive on $\mathrm{X}_i$. To confirm this note that by induction it suffices to prove the case $i=k-1$. Furthermore, it suffices to check that if $\eta_{k-1}(g)\pi_{k-1}(x)=\pi_{k-1}(x)$ for some $x\in \mathrm{X}$ and $g\in H$ then $\eta_{k-1}(g)=\mathrm{id}$. But the element $y:=gx$ then satisfies $x\sim_H y$ and $\pi_{k-1}(x)=\pi_{k-1}(y)$. By \eqref{eq:ft-fil} there is therefore some $g'\in H_k$ such that $y=g'x$. Since the action of $H$ is free, we conclude that $g=g'\in H_k$, so $\eta_{k-1}(g)=\mathrm{id}$ as required.
nodes.section: 5.3 Free groupable congruences and embeddings

nodes.name: Characterization of free fiber-transitive filtrations on free nilspaces
nodes.statement: Let $F$ be a $k$-step free nilspace, and let $H_\bullet$ be a subfiltration of $\Theta_\bullet(F)$. Then $H_\bullet$ is free fiber-transitive if and only if the following holds: for every $\alpha\in H$, with corresponding formula $\alpha(x_1,\ldots,x_k)=(x_1,\ldots,x_k)+(T_1,T_2(x_1),\ldots,T_k(x_1,\ldots,x_{k-1}))$, letting $i=i_\alpha\in[k]$ be the smallest integer such that $T_i\not=0$, the map $T_i$ is constant (with value in $\mathbb{Z}^{a_i}\times \mathbb{R}^{b_i}$).

nodes.label: lem:equi-strong-good

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 5.44

nodes.name: Forward implication
nodes.statement: Suppose that $H_\bullet$ is free fiber-transitive on $F$ and let $\alpha\in H$. Note that passing to the appropriate factor we can assume that $T_i=0$ for all $i\in[k-1]$ and $T_i\not=0$ (the constant 0 function). Then for every $x\in \mathrm{X}$ we have $\alpha(x)\sim_H x$ and $\pi_{k-1}(\alpha(x))=\pi_{k-1}(x)$. By  \eqref{eq:ft-fil} combined with the assumption that $H$ acts freely, this implies that $\alpha\in H_k$. By \cite[Lemma 3.2.37]{Cand:Notes1}, this in turn  implies that $T_k=c$ for some $c\in \mathbb{Z}^{a_{k}}\times \mathbb{R}^{b_{k}}$.

nodes.statement_short: Free action and ft-fil force $\alpha\in H_k$, so $T_k$ is constant.

nodes.name: Converse: fiber-transitivity
nodes.statement:
To prove the converse, first let us see that $(H,H_\bullet)$ is a fiber-transitive filtration. We prove this by induction on $k$,  noting that the case $k=0$ is trivial. For $k>0$, first assume that $x,y\in F$ are such that $\alpha(x)=y$ for some $\alpha\in H$ and $\pi_{k-1}(x)=\pi_{k-1}(y)$. Hence there exists $z\in \mathrm{Z}_k(F)$ such that $y=x+z=\alpha(x)$. By assumption on $(H,H_\bullet)$ note that $\alpha$ must be of the form $\alpha(x_1,\ldots,x_k)=(x_1,\ldots,x_k)+(0,\ldots,0,T_k(x_1,\ldots,x_{k-1}))$. The reason for this is that if $i=i_\alpha\in[k]$ is the first coordinate such that $T_i\not=0$ and $i<k$, then it is impossible that $\pi_{k-1}(x)=\pi_{k-1}(y)$, as $T_i$ would add a non-zero constant to a coordinate $i\in[k-1]$. Then note that the hypothesis on $H$ implies that $T_{k-1}=c$ for some constant $c\in \mathbb{Z}^{a_{k}}\times \mathbb{R}^{b_{k}}$. Thus $\alpha\in H_k$.

Now let us see how we can address the case $i<k$ by induction. If $\pi_i(x)=\pi_i(y)$ and $\alpha(x)=y$ for some $\alpha\in H$ we have in particular that $\alpha_{k-1}(\pi_{k-1}(x))=\pi_{k-1}(y)$. By induction on $k$, the filtration $(\eta_{k-1}(H_i))_{i\geq 0}$ is fiber-transitive on $\mathrm{X}_{k-1}$, so there exists $\beta_{k-1}=\eta_{k-1}(\beta)\in \eta_{k-1}(H_{i+1})$ such that $\beta_{k-1}(\pi_{k-1}(x))=\pi_{k-1}(y)$. Hence $\pi_{k-1}(\beta(x)) = \pi_{k-1}(y)$ and $\beta(x)\sim_H y$ (as $\beta(x)=\beta(\alpha^{-1}(\alpha(x))) = \beta(\alpha^{-1}(y))\sim_H y$). Thus, by the case of the previous paragraph applied to $\beta(x)\sim_H y$ we have that there exists $\gamma\in H_k$ such that $\beta(x)+\gamma=y$. As $\beta(\cdot)+\gamma\in H_{i+1}$ this concludes the proof.

nodes.name: Converse: freeness
nodes.statement:
In order to see that $(H,H_\bullet)$ is free fiber-transitive suppose that $\alpha,\beta\in H$ are such that $\alpha(x)=\beta(x)$ for some $x\in \mathrm{X}$. Assume for contradiction that these translations are not equal. Passing to some factor of $\mathrm{X}$ we can assume that
\[
\begin{cases}
 \alpha(x_1,\ldots,x_k)=(x_1,\ldots,x_k)+(T_1,T_2(x_1),\ldots,T_{k-1}(x_1,\ldots,x_{k-2}),T_k(x_1,\ldots,x_{k-1}))\\
 \beta(x_1,\ldots,x_k)=(x_1,\ldots,x_k)+(T_1,T_2(x_1),\ldots,T_{k-1}(x_1,\ldots,x_{k-2}),T'_k(x_1,\ldots,x_{k-1}))
\end{cases}
\]
for two distinct functions $T_k\not=T'_k$. Note that $\beta^{-1}\alpha$ must then be of the form $\beta^{-1}\alpha(x_1,\ldots,x_k)=(x_1,\ldots,x_k)+(0,\ldots,0,T''_k(x_1,\ldots,x_{k-1}))$ for some $T''_k\not=0$. However $\beta^{-1}\alpha(x)=x$ with $\beta^{-1}\alpha\in H$. By hypothesis we have that $T''=c$ for some constant $c\in \mathbb{Z}^{a_k}\times \mathbb{R}^{b_k}$. As $\beta^{-1}\alpha$ fixes $x$, this constant must be 0, so $T''_k=0$, a contradiction.

However $\beta^{-1}\alpha(x)=x$ with $\beta^{-1}\alpha\in H$. By hypothesis we have that $T''=c$ for some constant $c\in \mathbb{Z}^{a_k}\times \mathbb{R}^{b_k}$. nodes.statement_short: The difference is a constant fixing $x$, so zero.

nodes.name: Continuous closure of a free nilspace
nodes.statement: The \emph{continuous closure} of a free nilspace $F=\prod_{i=1}^k\mathcal{D}_i(\mathbb{Z}^{a_i})\times \mathcal{D}_i(\mathbb{R}^{b_i})$ is the nilspace $F^*=\prod_{i=1}^k\mathcal{D}_i(\mathbb{R}^{a_i})\times\mathcal{D}_i( \mathbb{R}^{b_i})$. The inclusion map $F\rightarrow F^*$ is a nilspace morphism.
nodes.section: 5.3 Free groupable congruences and embeddings
nodes.label: def:ctsclosure

nodes.name: Embedding of translation groups into the continuous closure
nodes.statement: By Theorem \ref{thm:decrip-trans-group} and \eqref{prop:lift-disc}, \eqref{prop:lift-cont}, it follows that there is an injective filtered homomorphism $\iota:\Theta(F)\rightarrow \Theta(F^*)$, consising simply in extending each polynomial involved in the expression \eqref{eq:str-trans-ab-nil} of a translation, and defined on a power of $\mathbb{Z}$, to the same polynomial defined on the same power of $\mathbb{R}$. Note that clearly for any $\alpha\in \Theta(F)$ and any $x\in F$ we have $\phi(\alpha(x))=\iota(\alpha)(\phi(x))$.
nodes.section: 5.3 Free groupable congruences and embeddings
conclusions: By Theorem \ref{thm:decrip-trans-group} and \eqref{prop:lift-disc}, \eqref{prop:lift-cont}, it follows that there is an injective filtered homomorphism $\iota:\Theta(F)\rightarrow \Theta(F^*)$, consising simply in extending each polynomial involved in the expression \eqref{eq:str-trans-ab-nil} of a translation, and defined on a power of $\mathbb{Z}$, to the same polynomial defined on the same power of $\mathbb{R}$.
Note that clearly for any $\alpha\in \Theta(F)$ and any $x\in F$ we have $\phi(\alpha(x))=\iota(\alpha)(\phi(x))$.

nodes.name: Embedding quotients of free nilspaces into toral nilspaces
nodes.statement: Let $F$ be a $k$-step free nilspace, and let $H_\bullet$ be a free fiber-transitive filtration on $F$ that is finitely-generated, fiber-discrete, and such that $\pi_H(F)$ is a compact nilspace. Then there exists a toral nilspace $\mathrm{X}$ and a continuous injective morphism from $\pi_H(F)$ into $\mathrm{X}$.
nodes.section: 5.3 Free groupable congruences and embeddings
assumptions: Let $F$ be a $k$-step free nilspace, and let $H_\bullet$ be a free fiber-transitive filtration on $F$ that is finitely-generated, fiber-discrete, and such that $\pi_H(F)$ is a compact nilspace.
conclusions: Then there exists a toral nilspace $\mathrm{X}$ and a continuous injective morphism from $\pi_H(F)$ into $\mathrm{X}$.
nodes.label: prop:embeb-strong-good

nodes.name: Embedding into connected nilmanifolds
nodes.statement: Recall from \cite[Theorem 2.9.17]{Cand:Notes2} that a toral nilspace is isomorphic to a compact connected filtered nilmanifold $(G/\Gamma,G_\bullet)$ equipped with the coset nilspace structure associated with $G_\bullet$. Thus, under the assumptions of Proposition \ref{prop:embeb-strong-good}, we can embed $\pi_H(F)$ as a \textsc{cfr} nilspace into a connected nilmanifold. See also Remark \ref{rem:2-step-embed} concerning the 2-step case.
nodes.section: 5.3 Free groupable congruences and embeddings

nodes.name: Toral nilspaces are connected nilmanifolds
nodes.statement: Recall from \cite[Theorem 2.9.17]{Cand:Notes2} that a toral nilspace is isomorphic to a compact connected filtered nilmanifold $(G/\Gamma,G_\bullet)$ equipped with the coset nilspace structure associated with $G_\bullet$.

conclusions: Recall from \cite[Theorem 2.9.17]{Cand:Notes2} that a toral nilspace is isomorphic to a compact connected filtered nilmanifold $(G/\Gamma,G_\bullet)$ equipped with the coset nilspace structure associated with $G_\bullet$.

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 5.46
nodes.statement: We want to prove that the natural inclusions $\phi:F\rightarrow F^*$ and $\iota:\Theta(F)\rightarrow \Theta(F^*)$ induce a well-defined continuous injective morphism $\varphi:\pi_H(F) \rightarrow \pi_{\iota(H)}(F^*)$, $\pi_H(x)\mapsto \pi_{\iota(H)}(\phi(x))$. Let us first note that $H_\bullet$ being free fiber-transitive implies that $(\iota(H_i))_{i\geq 0}$ is also free fiber-transitive, since the latter filtration satisfies the criterion in Lemma \ref{lem:equi-strong-good}. The map $\varphi$ is well-defined, indeed for any $x\in F$ and $\alpha\in H$ (thus $\alpha(x)\sim_H x$) we have $\varphi(\pi_H(\alpha(x)))=\pi_{\iota(H)}(\phi(\alpha(x)))=\pi_{\iota(H)}(\iota(\alpha)(\phi(x)))=\pi_{\iota(H)}(\phi(x))=\varphi(\pi_H(x))$. Moreover, Lemma \ref{lem:cong-equi} implies that $\varphi$ is a morphism, as cubes in $\pi_H(F)$ are of the form $\pi_H\circ\hspace{-0.02 cm} \mathrm{c}$ for $\mathrm{c}\in \mathrm{C}^n(F)$, whence $\varphi\circ\hspace{-0.02 cm} \pi_H\circ\hspace{-0.02 cm} \mathrm{c} = \pi_{\iota(H)}\circ\hspace{-0.02 cm} \phi\circ\hspace{-0.02 cm} \mathrm{c}\in \mathrm{C}^n(F^*/\sim_{\iota(H)})$. The injectivity of the map $\varphi$ is proved as follows: supposing that $\pi_{\iota(H)}(\phi(x)) = \pi_{\iota(H)}(\phi(y))$, there exists $\alpha\in H$ such that $\phi(y)=\iota(\alpha)(\phi(x))= \phi(\alpha(x))$, and since $\phi$ is injective we have $\alpha(x)=y$, so $\pi_H(x)=\pi_H(y)$. Hence $\varphi$ is indeed a morphism embedding $\pi_H(F)$ into the nilspace $\pi_{\iota(H)}(F^*)$. Finally we have to prove that $\pi_{\iota(H)}(F^*)$ is a toral nilspace. Since by assumption $\pi_H(F)$ is compact, its structure groups are the compact abelian groups $\mathrm{Z}_i(F)/\eta_i(H_i)$ for $i\in[k]$ (by Lemma \ref{lem:cong-equi}). By assumption $\eta_i(H_i)$ is a discrete cocompact subgroup pf $\mathrm{Z}_i(F)$. It is then easy to see that $\eta_i(\iota(H_i))$ is also a discrete cocompact subgroup of $\mathrm{Z}_i(F^*)$, so $\mathrm{Z}_i(F^*)/\eta_i(\iota(H_i))$ is a torus. Hence $\pi_{\iota(H)}(F^*)$ is a toral nilspace.
nodes.section: 5.3 Free groupable congruences and embeddings
nodes.statement_short: Extend polynomials from integer to real variables to map $\pi_H(F)$ injectively into $\pi_{\iota(H)}(F^*)$, whose structure groups are tori.

nodes.name: Isometric embedding into the toral nilspace
nodes.statement: The toral nilspace $\mathrm{X}$ in which we embed $\pi_H(F)$ can be endowed with an arbitrary metric that generates its topology. Given any such metric $d$ on $\mathrm{X}$, we can define a metric $d'$ on $\pi_H(F)$ simply by declaring $d'(x,y):=d(\varphi(x),\varphi(y))$. As $\varphi$ is a homeomorphism onto its image this is indeed a metric on $\pi_H(F)$. Relative to $d'$ and $d$, the map $\varphi$ is an isometry.
nodes.section: 5.3 Free groupable congruences and embeddings
nodes.label: rem:isometric-embedding

nodes.name: CFR nilspaces are quotients of free nilspaces by closed groupable congruences
nodes.statement: Let $\mathrm{X}$ be a $k$-step \textsc{cfr} nilspace. Then there exists a $k$-step free nilspace $F$ and a closed groupable congruence $\sim$ on $F$ such that $\pi_\sim(F)$, $\mathrm{X}$ are isomorphic as \textsc{cfr} nilspaces.

nodes.name: Representation of CFR nilspaces via fiber-transitive filtrations on free nilspaces
nodes.statement: Let $\mathrm{X}$ be a $k$-step \textsc{cfr} nilspace. Then there exists a $k$-step free nilspace $F$, and a fiber-transitive filtration $H_\bullet$ on $F$ which is finitely-generated, fiber-discrete and fiber-cocompact, such that $\pi_H(\mathrm{X})$ and $\mathrm{X}$ are isomorphic as \textsc{cfr} nilspaces.

nodes.name: Generators adapted to a filtration of a finitely generated nilpotent group
nodes.statement: Let $H$ be a $k$-step nilpotent finitely-generated group. Then for every filtration $H_\bullet=(H_i)_{i\ge 0}$ on $H$ there exist $h_1\ldots,h_n\in H$, and a subset $I_j\subset [n]$ for each $j\in[k]$, such that for every $j\in[k]$ we have $H_j=\langle h_{i}\rangle_{i\in I_j}$ .

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 6.3
nodes.statement: The group $H$ is Noetherian. Thus, every subgroup is finitely generated, and we can take as our set $h_1,\ldots,h_n\in H$ the union of all those generators for $j\in[k]$.
nodes.section: 6 \textsc{cfr} nilspaces as quotients of free nilspaces by groupable congruences
nodes.statement_short: Finitely generated nilpotent groups are Noetherian; collect generators of each filtration term.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 6.2
nodes.statement: We argue by induction on the step $k$. For $k=1$ the result follows from the standard theory of compact abelian Lie groups. Let $k>1$ and suppose by induction that $\mathrm{X}_{k-1}$ satisfies the theorem's conclusion, so there is a $(k-1)$-step free nilspace $F_{k-1}$, and a finitely-generated fiber-transitive filtration $H_\bullet$ on $F_{k-1}$, fiber-discrete and fiber-cocompact, with corresponding quotient map the fibration $\varphi_{k-1}:F_{k-1}\rightarrow\mathrm{X}_{k-1}$, such that the induced map $\overline{\varphi_{k-1}}:\pi_H(F_{k-1})\rightarrow \mathrm{X}_{k-1}$ is an isomorphism of compact nilspaces. Recall from \eqref{eq:etaj} the definition of the maps $\eta_j$. By Corollary \ref{cor:equivalent-filtrations} the filtration $(H\cap \Theta_j(F_{k-1}))_{j\ge 0}$ defines the same quotient nilspace as $H_\bullet$. By Corollary \ref{cor:same-last-str-gr} we then have $\eta_j(H_j)=\eta_j(H\cap \Theta_j(F_{k-1}))$ for every $j\in [k-1]$, so in particular for every such $j$ the group $\eta_j(H\cap \Theta_j(F_{k-1}))$ is discrete and cocompact in $\mathrm{Z}_j(F_{k-1})$. Hence, we can assume that the group $H$ is finitely-generated, fiber-discrete and fiber-cocompact when considered with filtration $\big(H\cap \Theta_j(F_{k-1})\big)_{j\geq 0}$, and that $\pi_H(F_{k-1})\cong \mathrm{X}_{k-1}$. By Lemma \ref{lem:noeth-group} there is a set $\{h_1,\ldots,h_n\}$ generating $H$ and such that for every $j\in[k]$ the subgroup $H\cap \Theta_j(F_{k-1})$ is generated by a subset of $\{h_1\ldots,h_n\}$. Hence, from now on we will assume that $H_j=H\cap \Theta_j(F_{k-1})$ for all $j\in[k]$ and that $H_j$ is generated by some elements in $\{h_1,\ldots,h_n\}$. Let us now consider the fiber product of $F_{k-1}$ and $\mathrm{X}$, i.e., the nilspace $\mathrm{Y}:= F_{k-1}\times_{\mathrm{X}_{k-1}}\mathrm{X}$ $=\{(f,x)\in F_{k-1}\times \mathrm{X}:\varphi_{k-1}(f)=\pi_{k-1}(x)\}$. This is a $k$-step Lie-fibered nilspace, by Lemma \ref{lem:fib-prod-top-nil}, and the following diagram commutes: \begin{equation} \begin{aligned}[c] \begin{tikzpicture} \matrix (m) [matrix of math nodes,row sep=3em,column sep=4em,minimum width=2em] {\mathrm{Y} & \mathrm{X} \\ F_{k-1} & \mathrm{X}_{k-1}, \\}; \path[-stealth] (m-1-1) edge node [above] {$p_2$} (m-1-2) (m-1-1) edge node [right] {$p_1$} (m-2-1) (m-1-2) edge node [right] {$\pi_{k-1}$} (m-2-2) (m-2-1) edge node [above] {$\varphi_{k-1}$} (m-2-2); \end{tikzpicture} \end{aligned} \end{equation} \vspace{-0.3cm} \noindent where $p_1:\mathrm{Y}\rightarrow F_{k-1}$, $(f,x)\mapsto f$ and $p_2:\mathrm{Y}\rightarrow \mathrm{X}$, $(f,x)\mapsto x$. It is checked straightforwardly that these maps are continuous fibrations. The proof of Lemma \ref{lem:fib-prod-top-nil} yields that $\mathrm{Y}$ is a degree-$k$ extension of $F_{k-1}$ by $\mathrm{Z}_k=\mathrm{Z}_k(\mathrm{X})$. By Theorem \ref{thm:splitext}, this extension splits. It follows that there is an isomorphism of \textsc{lch} nilspaces $\iota:\mathrm{Y}\rightarrow F_{k-1}\times \mathcal{D}_k(\mathrm{Z}_k)$. Let $\mathrm{Z}_k'$ be the covering group of $\mathrm{Z}_k$ involved in Theorem \ref{thm:lift-mor-cfr-ab-gr}, with corresponding covering homomorphism $\pi:\mathrm{Z}_k'\rightarrow \mathrm{Z}_k$. In particular $\mathrm{Z}_k'=\mathbb{R}^c\times \mathbb{Z}^b$ for some integers $c,b\ge 0$, and there is a lattice $\Gamma_k=\ker(\pi)\leq \mathrm{Z}_k'$ such that $\mathrm{Z}_k'/\Gamma_k\cong \mathrm{Z}_k$. We can now define the free nilspace $F$ in the theorem's conclusion: \begin{equation} F:= F_{k-1}\times \mathcal{D}_k(\mathrm{Z}_k'). \end{equation} We define also the nilspace fibration $\phi:F \rightarrow F_{k-1}\times \mathcal{D}_k(\mathrm{Z}_k), \; (f,z')\mapsto \big(f,\pi(z')\big)$. Next, we observe that every translation $h\in \compl{H}\cap \Theta_i(F_{k-1})$ (in particular every $h\in H_i$) yields a translation $\tilde{h}\in \Theta_i(\mathrm{Y})$ defined by $\tilde{h}(f,x) = (h(f),x)$. Indeed, we have firstly that $\tilde{h}$ is $\mathrm{Y}$-valued, because since $\pi_H(f)=\pi_{k-1}(x)$ and $h$ is $\sim_{H}$-vertical, we also have $\pi_{H}(h(f))=\pi_{k-1}(x)$, so $ (h(f),x)\in \mathrm{Y}$. Secondly $\tilde{h}\in \Theta_i(\mathrm{Y})$, indeed for any $n$-cube $\mathrm{c}_1\times\mathrm{c}_2$ on $\mathrm{Y}$, and any $i$-codimensional face $E \subset \db{n}$, we have $h^{E}\cdot \mathrm{c}_1\in \mathrm{C}^n(F)$ and $\pi_H\circ\hspace{-0.02 cm} (h^{E}\cdot \mathrm{c}_1) =\pi_H\circ\hspace{-0.02 cm} \mathrm{c}_1=\pi_{k-1}\circ\hspace{-0.02 cm} \mathrm{c}_2$, so $(h^{E}\cdot \mathrm{c}_1)\times\mathrm{c}_2\in \mathrm{C}^n(\mathrm{Y})$. Recalling the notation from \cite[Lemma 1.5]{CGSS} we let $\widehat{\iota}:\Theta(\mathrm{Y})\rightarrow \Theta(F_{k-1}\times \mathcal{D}_k(\mathrm{Z}_k))$ be the group isomorphism (in particular filtered homomorphism) induced by the nilspace isomorphism $\iota$. It is then checked straightforwardly that the map $\psi:H\rightarrow \Theta\big(F_{k-1}\times \mathcal{D}_k(\mathrm{Z}_k)\big)$, $h\mapsto \widehat{\iota}(\tilde h)$ is an injective filtered homomorphism mapping $H_\bullet$ onto a fiber-transitive filtration on $F_{k-1}\times \mathcal{D}_k(\mathrm{Z}_k)$, whose corresponding quotient is isomorphic to $\mathrm{X}$. Our aim now is to lift the filtration $\psi(H_\bullet)$ through $\phi$ to a fiber-transitive filtration on $F$ satisfying the theorem's conclusion. We shall do this by lifting the generators $\psi(h_i)$. By Theorem \ref{thm:lift-trans}, for every $\alpha\in \Theta_j(F_{k-1}\times \mathcal{D}_k(\mathrm{Z}_k))$ there exists a lift $\alpha'$ of $\alpha$ through $\phi$, i.e.\ a (possibly non-unique) $\alpha'\in \Theta_j(F)$ such that $\phi\circ\hspace{-0.02 cm} \alpha' = \alpha\circ\hspace{-0.02 cm}\phi$. For each $i\in[n]$, we thus choose some lift $h'_i\in \Theta(F)$ of $\psi(h_i)$ through $\phi$, and we do so using the filtered-homomorphism property of $\psi$ in such a way that, if $j$ is the greatest index in $[k]$ such that $h_i\in H_j$, then $h_i'\in \Theta_j(F)$ (this will be used below to establish the fiber-transitivity property for the group generated by these lifts). The lattice $\Gamma_k=\ker(\pi)$ is finitely generated, so let $z_1,\ldots,z_t\in \mathrm{Z}_k'$ form a generating set for $\Gamma_k$. Then for every $s\in[t]$ let $\gamma_s\in \Theta_k(F)$ be the map $\gamma_s(f,a'):=(f,a'+z_s)$ (recall that $(f,a')\in F=F_{k-1}\times \mathcal{D}_k(\mathrm{Z}_k')$). We claim that the filtered group $\big(H':=\langle h_1'\ldots,h_n',\gamma_1,\ldots,\gamma_t\rangle,\; H'_\bullet:=(H'\cap\Theta_i(F))_{i\geq 0}\big)$, together with the map $\varphi:=p_2\circ\hspace{-0.02 cm} \iota^{-1}\circ\hspace{-0.02 cm} \phi: F\rightarrow \mathrm{X}$, satisfy the conclusion of the theorem. To prove this, we first note that the map $\phi:F\rightarrow F_{k-1}\times \mathcal{D}_k(\mathrm{Z}_k)$ is $\Theta(F)$-consistent in the sense of \cite[Definition 1.2]{CGSS}, i.e.\ for every $\alpha\in \Theta(F)$, if $\phi((f,z))=\phi((f',z'))$ then $\phi(\alpha(f,z))=\phi(\alpha(f',z'))$. Indeed $\phi((f,z))=\phi((f',z'))$ implies that $f'=f$ and that $\pi(z)=\pi(z')$ (i.e.\ $z,z'$ are equal modulo $\Gamma_k$); the equality $f'=f$ implies (using the description \eqref{eq:str-trans-ab-nil} and the fact that the factor map $\pi_{k-1,F}:F\rightarrow F_{k-1}$ is simply the projection $(f,a')\mapsto f$) that $\alpha(f,z)$, $\alpha(f',z')$ are equal modulo $\pi_{k-1,F}$ and that their $k$-th step components are respectively $z+t,z'+t$ for some $t\in \mathrm{Z}_k'$ depending on $\alpha$ and $f=f'$. Hence $\phi(\alpha(f',z'))$, $\phi(\alpha(f,z))$ have equal $\pi_{k-1}$ projection and $k$-th component respectively $\pi(z'+t),\pi(z+t)$, also equal, so $\phi(\alpha(f,z))=\phi(\alpha(f',z'))$ as claimed. Thus by \cite[Lemma 1.5]{CGSS} we have a well-defined filtered homomorphism $\widehat{\phi}:\Theta(F)\rightarrow \Theta(F_{k-1}\times \mathcal{D}_k(\mathrm{Z}_k))$, $\alpha\mapsto \big((f,\pi(z))\mapsto \phi (\alpha(f,z))\big)$. Now a simple computation shows that $\pi_{k-1,F}$ equals the map $p_1\circ\hspace{-0.02 cm} \iota^{-1}\circ\hspace{-0.02 cm} \phi$. Let $\eta_{k-1}:\Theta(F)\rightarrow \Theta(F_{k-1})$ be the corresponding homomorphism as defined in \eqref{eq:etaj}. We then have the following fact, which we will use to obtain part of the fiber-transitive property by induction below, as well as the required topological properties thereafter: \begin{equation} \textrm{$\eta_{k-1}(H'_j)=H_j$ for every $j\in [k-1]$.} \end{equation} To see this note that by construction $\eta_{k-1}(H'_j)$ contains all the generators of $H_j$, so $\eta_{k-1}(H'_j)\supset H_j$, and since clearly $\eta_{k-1}(\gamma_i)=\mathrm{id}$ for all $i\in[t]$ (as $\gamma_i\in\Theta_k(F)$), we deduce \eqref{eq:filtcorresp}. In addition to \eqref{eq:filtcorresp}, we also need the following description of $H_k'$ (where $\Gamma_k=\ker(\pi)$ is identified with the subgroup of $\Theta(F)$ consisting of translations $f\mapsto f+z$ for $z\in \Gamma_k$): \begin{equation} H'_k:=H'\cap \Theta_k(F) = \Gamma_k. \end{equation} The inclusion $\Gamma_k\subset H'\cap \Theta_k(F)$ is clear since the elements $\gamma_s$ generating $\Gamma_k$ are all in $\Theta_k(F)\cap H'$ by construction, so we prove the opposite inclusion. Every element $\alpha\in \Theta_k(F)$ is of the form $(f,a')\mapsto(f,a'+z)$ for some $z\in \mathrm{Z}_k'$, so we have to prove that if $\alpha=h'\in H'$ then $z\in \Gamma_k$. As an element of $\Theta(F_{k-1})$, the translation $\eta_{k-1}(h')$ acts on $\mathrm{Y}=F_{k-1}\times_{\mathrm{X}_{k-1}}\mathrm{X}$ via the first component, so we have on one hand that $\widehat{\iota^{-1}}(\widehat{\phi}(h'))$ maps every $(f,x)\in F_{k-1}\times_{\mathrm{X}_{k-1}}\mathrm{X}$ to $(\eta_{k-1}(h')f,x)$. On the other hand, since $h':(f,a')\mapsto (f,a'+z)$, we see by developing the definitions that the map $\widehat{\iota^{-1}}(\widehat{\phi}(h'))$ must take every $(f,x)\in \mathrm{Y}$ to $(f,x+\pi(z))$. Thus for all $(f,x)\in \mathrm{Y}$ we have $(\eta_{k-1}(h')f,x)=(f,x+\pi(z))$. Composing with $p_2$ we conclude that $z\in \ker(\pi)= \Gamma_k$, yielding the required inclusion. Now let us prove that the filtration $H'_\bullet$ is fiber-transitive on $F$. First let us see that if $\pi_{k-1}(f_1,a_1')=\pi_{k-1}(f_2,a'_2)$ and $\alpha(f_1,a_1')=(f_2,a'_2)$ for some $\alpha\in H$ then we can find $z\in \Gamma_k=H'\cap\Theta_k(F)$ such that $(f_1,a'_1)+z=(f_2,a'_2)$. Recall that $\pi_{k-1}:F\rightarrow F_{k-1}$ is the map $(f,a')\mapsto p_1(\iota^{-1}(\phi(f,a')))=f$. Thus $f_1=f_2$ and there exists $z\in \mathrm{Z}_k'$ such that $a_1'+z=a_2'$. But also, as $\alpha=\alpha^{d_1}_1\cdots \alpha^{d_\ell}_\ell$ we have that $\iota^{-1}(\phi(f_2,a_2')) = \iota^{-1}(\phi(\alpha(f_1,a_1'))) = (\beta^{d_1}_1\cdots \beta^{d_\ell}_\ell(f_1),x(f_1,a_1')) $ where $\beta_u$ are again either some $h_i$ or the identity and $x(f_1,a_1')\in \mathrm{X}$ is such that $\iota^{-1}(\phi(f_1,a_1'))=(f_1,x(f_1,a_1'))$. As computed before, we have $\beta^{d_1}_1\cdots \beta^{d_\ell}_\ell(f_1) = f_1$. Composing with $\iota$ in the equality $\iota^{-1}(\phi(f_2,a'_2))=(f_1,x(f_1,a_1'))$ we have that $(f_2,a_2'\mod \Gamma_k)=(f_1,a_1'\mod\Gamma_k)$. So in particular $z\in \Gamma_k$ and we have found that $(f_1,a_1')+z=(f_2,a_2')$ for some $z\in \Gamma_k=H'\cap \Theta_k(F)$. Now, let $\alpha(f_1,a_1')=(f_2,a_2')$ and $\pi_j(f_1,a_1')=\pi_j(f_2,a_2')$ for $j<k-1$. In particular, $\pi_j(f_1)=\pi_j(f_2)$ and $h(f_1)=f_2$ for some $h\in H$ (here, abusing the notation we indicate by $\pi_j$ the projection to the $j$-th factor, either from $F$ or from $F_{k-1}$). By hypothesis on $H$ there exists an element $h^*\in H_{j+1}$ such that $h^*(f_1)=f_2$. By definition, there exists then some $\tau\in H'_{j+1}$ such that $\pi_{k-1}(\tau(f_1,a_1)) = h^*(f_1)$ (just write $h^*$ in terms of the fixed generators $h_i$ and lift these one by one, using the above-mentioned guarantee that if $h_i\in H_{j+1}$, then $h_i'\in H'_{j+1}$). Then, we have that $\pi_{k-1}(\tau(f_1,a_1))=\pi_{k-1}(f_2,a'_2)$ and clearly they differ in an element of $H'$. By the previous paragraph we have that there exists $\gamma\in \Gamma_k$ such that $\gamma(\tau(f_1,a'_1))=(f_2,a_2')$, which concludes the proof. For the topological aspects, note that the map $\pi_{H'}(f,a')\mapsto \varphi(f,a')=p_2(\iota^{-1}(\phi(f,a')))$ factors through $\pi_H$, and as $\varphi$ is continuous and $\pi_H$ is an open quotient map, the map $\overline{\varphi}\circ\hspace{-0.02 cm} \pi_H:=\varphi$ is continuous. By \eqref{eq:filtcorresp}, \eqref{eq:filtcorresp-2}, and induction on the step it follows that $H'$ is also fiber-discrete and fiber-cocompact. By Corollary \ref{cor:quo-cfr-nil} we know that $\pi_{H'}(F)$ is a compact nilspace. A simple computation yields that indeed $\overline{\varphi}$ is bijective. Hence, being the bijection between compact Hausdorff spaces it is a homeomorphism. Both $\overline{\varphi}$ and $\overline{\varphi}^{-1}$ can be checked to be morphisms which concludes the proof.

nodes.name: Inductive hypothesis and normalization
nodes.statement: Let $k>1$ and suppose by induction that $\mathrm{X}_{k-1}$ satisfies the theorem's conclusion, so there is a $(k-1)$-step free nilspace $F_{k-1}$, and a finitely-generated fiber-transitive filtration $H_\bullet$ on $F_{k-1}$, fiber-discrete and fiber-cocompact, with corresponding quotient map the fibration $\varphi_{k-1}:F_{k-1}\rightarrow\mathrm{X}_{k-1}$, such that the induced map $\overline{\varphi_{k-1}}:\pi_H(F_{k-1})\rightarrow \mathrm{X}_{k-1}$ is an isomorphism of compact nilspaces. Recall from \eqref{eq:etaj} the definition of the maps $\eta_j$. By Corollary \ref{cor:equivalent-filtrations}  the filtration $(H\cap \Theta_j(F_{k-1}))_{j\ge 0}$ defines the same quotient nilspace as $H_\bullet$.  By Corollary \ref{cor:same-last-str-gr} we then have  $\eta_j(H_j)=\eta_j(H\cap \Theta_j(F_{k-1}))$ for every $j\in [k-1]$, so in particular for every such $j$ the group $\eta_j(H\cap \Theta_j(F_{k-1}))$ is discrete and cocompact in $\mathrm{Z}_j(F_{k-1})$. Hence, we can assume that the group $H$ is finitely-generated, fiber-discrete and fiber-cocompact when considered with filtration $\big(H\cap \Theta_j(F_{k-1})\big)_{j\geq 0}$, and that $\pi_H(F_{k-1})\cong \mathrm{X}_{k-1}$. By Lemma \ref{lem:noeth-group} there is a set $\{h_1,\ldots,h_n\}$ generating $H$ and such that for every $j\in[k]$ the subgroup $H\cap \Theta_j(F_{k-1})$ is generated by a subset of $\{h_1\ldots,h_n\}$. Hence, from now on we will assume that $H_j=H\cap \Theta_j(F_{k-1})$ for all $j\in[k]$ and that $H_j$ is generated by some elements in $\{h_1,\ldots,h_n\}$.

nodes.statement: The proof of Lemma \ref{lem:fib-prod-top-nil}  yields that $\mathrm{Y}$ is a degree-$k$ extension of $F_{k-1}$ by $\mathrm{Z}_k=\mathrm{Z}_k(\mathrm{X})$. By Theorem \ref{thm:splitext}, this extension splits. It follows that there is an isomorphism of \textsc{lch}  nilspaces $\iota:\mathrm{Y}\rightarrow F_{k-1}\times \mathcal{D}_k(\mathrm{Z}_k)$.

nodes.name: Transport $H$ to $\mathrm{Y}$
nodes.statement:
Next, we observe that every translation $h\in \compl{H}\cap \Theta_i(F_{k-1})$ (in particular every $h\in H_i$) yields a translation $\tilde{h}\in \Theta_i(\mathrm{Y})$ defined by
$\tilde{h}(f,x) = (h(f),x)$. Indeed, we have firstly that $\tilde{h}$ is $\mathrm{Y}$-valued, because since $\pi_H(f)=\pi_{k-1}(x)$ and $h$ is $\sim_{H}$-vertical, we also have $\pi_{H}(h(f))=\pi_{k-1}(x)$, so $ (h(f),x)\in \mathrm{Y}$. Secondly $\tilde{h}\in \Theta_i(\mathrm{Y})$, indeed for any $n$-cube $\mathrm{c}_1\times\mathrm{c}_2$ on $\mathrm{Y}$, and any $i$-codimensional face $E \subset \db{n}$, we have $h^{E}\cdot \mathrm{c}_1\in \mathrm{C}^n(F)$ and $\pi_H\circ\hspace{-0.02 cm} (h^{E}\cdot \mathrm{c}_1) =\pi_H\circ\hspace{-0.02 cm} \mathrm{c}_1=\pi_{k-1}\circ\hspace{-0.02 cm} \mathrm{c}_2$, so  $(h^{E}\cdot \mathrm{c}_1)\times\mathrm{c}_2\in \mathrm{C}^n(\mathrm{Y})$. Recalling the notation from \cite[Lemma 1.5]{CGSS} we let $\widehat{\iota}:\Theta(\mathrm{Y})\rightarrow \Theta(F_{k-1}\times \mathcal{D}_k(\mathrm{Z}_k))$ be the group isomorphism (in particular filtered homomorphism) induced by the nilspace isomorphism $\iota$. It is then checked straightforwardly that the map $\psi:H\rightarrow \Theta\big(F_{k-1}\times \mathcal{D}_k(\mathrm{Z}_k)\big)$, $h\mapsto \widehat{\iota}(\tilde h)$ is an injective filtered homomorphism mapping $H_\bullet$ onto a fiber-transitive filtration on $F_{k-1}\times \mathcal{D}_k(\mathrm{Z}_k)$, whose corresponding quotient is isomorphic to $\mathrm{X}$.
nodes.section: 6 \textsc{cfr} nilspaces as quotients of free nilspaces by groupable congruences
nodes.statement_short: Vertical translations act on the first coordinate.

nodes.name: Lift the generators
nodes.statement:
Our aim now is to lift the filtration $\psi(H_\bullet)$ through $\phi$ to a fiber-transitive filtration on $F$ satisfying the theorem's conclusion. We shall do this by lifting the generators $\psi(h_i)$. By Theorem \ref{thm:lift-trans}, for every $\alpha\in \Theta_j(F_{k-1}\times \mathcal{D}_k(\mathrm{Z}_k))$ there exists a lift $\alpha'$ of $\alpha$ through $\phi$, i.e.\ a (possibly non-unique) $\alpha'\in \Theta_j(F)$ such that $\phi\circ\hspace{-0.02 cm} \alpha' = \alpha\circ\hspace{-0.02 cm}\phi$. For each $i\in[n]$, we thus choose some lift $h'_i\in \Theta(F)$ of $\psi(h_i)$ through $\phi$, and we do so using the filtered-homomorphism property of $\psi$ in such a way that, if $j$ is the greatest index in $[k]$ such that $h_i\in H_j$, then $h_i'\in \Theta_j(F)$ (this will be used below to establish the fiber-transitivity property  for the group generated by these lifts).

The lattice $\Gamma_k=\ker(\pi)$ is finitely generated, so let $z_1,\ldots,z_t\in \mathrm{Z}_k'$ form a generating set for $\Gamma_k$. Then for every $s\in[t]$ let $\gamma_s\in \Theta_k(F)$ be the map $\gamma_s(f,a'):=(f,a'+z_s)$  (recall that $(f,a')\in F=F_{k-1}\times \mathcal{D}_k(\mathrm{Z}_k')$).

nodes.name: $\phi$ is translation-consistent
nodes.statement:
To prove this, we first note that the map $\phi:F\rightarrow F_{k-1}\times \mathcal{D}_k(\mathrm{Z}_k)$ is $\Theta(F)$-consistent in the sense of \cite[Definition 1.2]{CGSS}, i.e.\ for every $\alpha\in \Theta(F)$, if $\phi((f,z))=\phi((f',z'))$ then $\phi(\alpha(f,z))=\phi(\alpha(f',z'))$. 
Indeed $\phi((f,z))=\phi((f',z'))$ implies that $f'=f$ and that $\pi(z)=\pi(z')$ (i.e.\ $z,z'$ are equal modulo $\Gamma_k$); the equality $f'=f$ implies (using the description \eqref{eq:str-trans-ab-nil} and the fact that the factor map $\pi_{k-1,F}:F\rightarrow F_{k-1}$ is simply the projection $(f,a')\mapsto f$) that  $\alpha(f,z)$, $\alpha(f',z')$ are equal modulo $\pi_{k-1,F}$ and that their $k$-th step components are respectively $z+t,z'+t$ for some $t\in \mathrm{Z}_k'$ depending on $\alpha$ and $f=f'$. Hence $\phi(\alpha(f',z'))$, $\phi(\alpha(f,z))$ have equal $\pi_{k-1}$ projection and $k$-th component respectively $\pi(z'+t),\pi(z+t)$, also equal, so $\phi(\alpha(f,z))=\phi(\alpha(f',z'))$ as claimed. Thus by \cite[Lemma 1.5]{CGSS} we have a well-defined filtered homomorphism $\widehat{\phi}:\Theta(F)\rightarrow \Theta(F_{k-1}\times \mathcal{D}_k(\mathrm{Z}_k))$, $\alpha\mapsto \big((f,\pi(z))\mapsto \phi (\alpha(f,z))\big)$.

nodes.label: eq:filtcorresp

nodes.name: Top term is the lattice
nodes.statement:
In addition to \eqref{eq:filtcorresp}, we also need the following description of $H_k'$ (where 
$\Gamma_k=\ker(\pi)$ is identified with the subgroup of $\Theta(F)$ consisting of translations $f\mapsto f+z$ for $z\in \Gamma_k$):
\begin{equation} H'_k:=H'\cap \Theta_k(F) = \Gamma_k.
\end{equation}
The inclusion $\Gamma_k\subset H'\cap \Theta_k(F)$ is clear since the elements $\gamma_s$ generating $\Gamma_k$ are all in $\Theta_k(F)\cap H'$ by construction, so we prove the opposite inclusion. Every element $\alpha\in \Theta_k(F)$ is of the form $(f,a')\mapsto(f,a'+z)$ for some $z\in \mathrm{Z}_k'$, so we have to prove that if $\alpha=h'\in H'$ then $z\in \Gamma_k$. As an element of $\Theta(F_{k-1})$, the translation $\eta_{k-1}(h')$ acts on $\mathrm{Y}=F_{k-1}\times_{\mathrm{X}_{k-1}}\mathrm{X}$ via the first component, so we have on one hand that $\widehat{\iota^{-1}}(\widehat{\phi}(h'))$  maps every $(f,x)\in  F_{k-1}\times_{\mathrm{X}_{k-1}}\mathrm{X}$ to $(\eta_{k-1}(h')f,x)$. On the other hand, since $h':(f,a')\mapsto (f,a'+z)$, we see by developing the definitions that the map $\widehat{\iota^{-1}}(\widehat{\phi}(h'))$ must take every $(f,x)\in \mathrm{Y}$ to $(f,x+\pi(z))$. Thus for all $(f,x)\in \mathrm{Y}$ we have $(\eta_{k-1}(h')f,x)=(f,x+\pi(z))$. Composing with $p_2$ we conclude that $z\in \ker(\pi)= \Gamma_k$, yielding the required inclusion.

nodes.statement:
In addition to \eqref{eq:filtcorresp}, we also need the following description of $H_k'$ (where

\begin{equation} H'_k:=H'\cap \Theta_k(F) = \Gamma_k.
\end{equation}
The inclusion $\Gamma_k\subset H'\cap \Theta_k(F)$ is clear since the elements $\gamma_s$ generating $\Gamma_k$ are all in $\Theta_k(F)\cap H'$ by construction, so we prove the opposite inclusion.

nodes.name: Reverse inclusion
nodes.statement: Every element $\alpha\in \Theta_k(F)$ is of the form $(f,a')\mapsto(f,a'+z)$ for some $z\in \mathrm{Z}_k'$, so we have to prove that if $\alpha=h'\in H'$ then $z\in \Gamma_k$. As an element of $\Theta(F_{k-1})$, the translation $\eta_{k-1}(h')$ acts on $\mathrm{Y}=F_{k-1}\times_{\mathrm{X}_{k-1}}\mathrm{X}$ via the first component, so we have on one hand that $\widehat{\iota^{-1}}(\widehat{\phi}(h'))$  maps every $(f,x)\in  F_{k-1}\times_{\mathrm{X}_{k-1}}\mathrm{X}$ to $(\eta_{k-1}(h')f,x)$. Thus for all $(f,x)\in \mathrm{Y}$ we have $(\eta_{k-1}(h')f,x)=(f,x+\pi(z))$. Composing with $p_2$ we conclude that $z\in \ker(\pi)= \Gamma_k$, yielding the required inclusion.

nodes.name: Fiber-transitivity of $H'_\bullet$
nodes.statement:
Now let us prove that the filtration $H'_\bullet$ is fiber-transitive on $F$. First let us see that if $\pi_{k-1}(f_1,a_1')=\pi_{k-1}(f_2,a'_2)$ and $\alpha(f_1,a_1')=(f_2,a'_2)$ for some $\alpha\in H$ then we can find $z\in \Gamma_k=H'\cap\Theta_k(F)$ such that $(f_1,a'_1)+z=(f_2,a'_2)$. Recall that  $\pi_{k-1}:F\rightarrow F_{k-1}$ is the map $(f,a')\mapsto p_1(\iota^{-1}(\phi(f,a')))=f$. Thus $f_1=f_2$ and there exists $z\in \mathrm{Z}_k'$ such that $a_1'+z=a_2'$. But also, as $\alpha=\alpha^{d_1}_1\cdots \alpha^{d_\ell}_\ell$ we have that $\iota^{-1}(\phi(f_2,a_2')) = \iota^{-1}(\phi(\alpha(f_1,a_1'))) = (\beta^{d_1}_1\cdots \beta^{d_\ell}_\ell(f_1),x(f_1,a_1')) $ where $\beta_u$ are again either some $h_i$ or the identity and $x(f_1,a_1')\in \mathrm{X}$ is such that $\iota^{-1}(\phi(f_1,a_1'))=(f_1,x(f_1,a_1'))$. As computed before, we have $\beta^{d_1}_1\cdots \beta^{d_\ell}_\ell(f_1) = f_1$. Composing with $\iota$ in the equality $\iota^{-1}(\phi(f_2,a'_2))=(f_1,x(f_1,a_1'))$ we have that $(f_2,a_2'\mod \Gamma_k)=(f_1,a_1'\mod\Gamma_k)$. So in particular $z\in \Gamma_k$ and we have found that $(f_1,a_1')+z=(f_2,a_2')$ for some $z\in \Gamma_k=H'\cap \Theta_k(F)$.

Now, let $\alpha(f_1,a_1')=(f_2,a_2')$ and $\pi_j(f_1,a_1')=\pi_j(f_2,a_2')$ for $j<k-1$. In particular, $\pi_j(f_1)=\pi_j(f_2)$ and $h(f_1)=f_2$ for some $h\in H$ (here, abusing the notation we indicate by $\pi_j$ the projection to the $j$-th factor, either from $F$ or from $F_{k-1}$). By hypothesis on $H$ there exists an element $h^*\in H_{j+1}$ such that $h^*(f_1)=f_2$. By definition, there exists then some $\tau\in H'_{j+1}$ such that $\pi_{k-1}(\tau(f_1,a_1)) = h^*(f_1)$ (just write $h^*$ in terms of the fixed generators $h_i$ and lift these one by one, using the above-mentioned guarantee that if $h_i\in H_{j+1}$, then $h_i'\in H'_{j+1}$). Then, we have that $\pi_{k-1}(\tau(f_1,a_1))=\pi_{k-1}(f_2,a'_2)$ and clearly they differ in an element of $H'$. By the previous paragraph we have that there exists $\gamma\in \Gamma_k$ such that $\gamma(\tau(f_1,a'_1))=(f_2,a_2')$, which concludes the proof.

nodes.name: Topological properties and isomorphism
nodes.statement: For the topological aspects, note that the map $\pi_{H'}(f,a')\mapsto \varphi(f,a')=p_2(\iota^{-1}(\phi(f,a')))$ factors through $\pi_H$, and as $\varphi$ is continuous and $\pi_H$ is an open quotient map, the map $\overline{\varphi}\circ\hspace{-0.02 cm} \pi_H:=\varphi$ is continuous. By \eqref{eq:filtcorresp}, \eqref{eq:filtcorresp-2}, and induction on the step it follows that $H'$ is also fiber-discrete and fiber-cocompact. By Corollary \ref{cor:quo-cfr-nil} we know that $\pi_{H'}(F)$ is a compact nilspace. A simple computation yields that indeed $\overline{\varphi}$ is bijective. nodes.name: Two-step case gives free fiber-transitive filtrations
nodes.statement: In the case $k=2$ of Theorem \ref{thm:groupequivrep}, the filtration $H_\bullet$ is free fiber-transitive.
nodes.section: 6 \textsc{cfr} nilspaces as quotients of free nilspaces by groupable congruences
assumptions: In the case $k=2$ of Theorem \ref{thm:groupequivrep}
conclusions: the filtration $H_\bullet$ is free fiber-transitive

nodes.name: Proof of Corollary 6.4
nodes.statement: Using the same notation as for Theorem \ref{thm:groupequivrep}, by construction we can take $F=\mathcal{D}_1(\mathrm{Z}_1')\times \mathcal{D}_2(\mathrm{Z}_2')$ and take $H'=\langle h_1',\ldots,h_n',\gamma_1,\ldots,\gamma_t\rangle$ where $h_1',\ldots,h_n'$ are lifts of the translations that freely generate the lattice $\eta_1(H')\subset \mathrm{Z}_1'$. Using that $H'_\bullet$ is of degree 2 and that the elements $\gamma_i$ generate $H_2'$, we deduce that every element of $H'$ can be written as ${h_1'}^{a_1}\cdots{h_n'}^{a_n}\gamma_1^{b_1}\cdots\gamma^{b_t}_t$ for integers $a_i,b_j\in \mathbb{Z}$, $i\in[n]$ and $j\in[t]$. By Theorem \ref{thm:decrip-trans-group} any translation on $F$ has the form $(x,y)\in \mathrm{Z}_1'\times \mathrm{Z}_2'\mapsto (x+c,y+d+T(x))$ where $T:\mathcal{D}_1(\mathrm{Z}_1')\rightarrow \mathcal{D}_1(\mathrm{Z}_2')$ is a morphism, $c\in \mathrm{Z}_1'$ and $d\in \mathrm{Z}_2'$. Moreover, the elements $\gamma_j$ only add a fixed constant to $\mathrm{Z}_2'$. Now we check that the condition for free-transitivity given in Lemma \ref{lem:equi-strong-good} holds. Given any $\alpha={h_1'}^{a_1}\cdots{h_n'}^{a_n}\gamma_1^{b_1}\cdots\gamma^{b_t}_t\in H'$, viewed as the map $\alpha(x,y)=(x+c,y+d+T(x))$, there are two cases. Firstly, if $c\not=0$ then the condition in Lemma \ref{lem:equi-strong-good} holds with $i_\alpha=1$. If $c=0$ then clearly $a_1=\cdots=a_n=0$, as $\eta_1(h_1'),\ldots,\eta_n(h_n')$ freely generate the lattice $\eta_1(H')$. In this case, the condition in Lemma \ref{lem:equi-strong-good} holds with $i_\alpha=2$.

nodes.name: Embedding 2-step CFR nilspaces into nilmanifolds
nodes.statement: Corollary \ref{cor:k=2-str-good} and Proposition \ref{prop:embeb-strong-good} together imply that any 2-step \textsc{cfr} nilspace can be embedded into a coset nilspace corresponding to a 2-step connected nilmanifold. This will enable us to recover and extend a recent inverse theorem of Jamneshan and Tao \cite{J&T} for the Gowers $U^3$-norm on finite abelian groups; see Theorem \ref{thm:jam-tao}. Note that a version of the above embedding result was proved for finite 2-step nilspaces by Host and Kra in \cite[Theorem 3]{HK-par}.

nodes.name: Smoothness of Lie-fibered nilspaces
nodes.statement: From Theorem \ref{thm:groupequivrep} it can be proved that $k$-step Lie-fibered nilspaces are in fact (real) $C^\infty$ manifolds. Also, for all $n\in \mathbb{N}$, $\mathrm{C}^n(\mathrm{X})$ is a $C^\infty$ manifold. And if $\varphi:\mathrm{X}\rightarrow \mathrm{Y}$ is a continuous morphism between $k$-step Lie-fibered nilspaces, it can also be proved that $\varphi$ is automatically $C^\infty$. As we do not need these results for the sequel, we omit their proofs.

nodes.name: Double-coset space
nodes.statement: Given a filtered group $(G,G_\bullet)$ and two subgroups $K,\Gamma$ of $G$, the \emph{double-coset space} $K\backslash G /\Gamma$ is the set of double cosets $K g \Gamma= \{kg\gamma:k\in K,\gamma\in \Gamma\}$, $g\in G$.
nodes.section: 7 Double-coset nilspaces

nodes.name: Double-coset nilspace
nodes.statement: Let $(G,G_\bullet)$ be a filtered group let $K,\Gamma$ be subgroups of $G$. The associated \emph{double-coset nilspace} is the double-coset space $K\backslash G /\Gamma$ together with the cubes of the form $K\mathrm{c} \Gamma: \db{n}\rightarrow K\backslash G /\Gamma$, $v \mapsto K\mathrm{c}(v)\Gamma$ (for $\mathrm{c}\in\mathrm{C}^n(G_\bullet)$).

nodes.name: Nilpair
nodes.statement: Let $(G,G_\bullet)$ be a degree-$k$ filtered group, let $\mathrm{X}$ be the associated group nilspace, and let $K,\Gamma$ be subgroups of $G$. We say that $(K,\Gamma)$ is a \emph{nilpair} in $(G,G_\bullet)$ if the equivalence relation on $G$ defined by $g_1\sim g_2 \iff Kg_1\Gamma=Kg_2\Gamma$ is a nilspace congruence on $\mathrm{X}$ and the quotient map $G\rightarrow K\backslash G /\Gamma$ is a nilspace fibration.
nodes.section: 7 Double-coset nilspaces

nodes.name: Groupable action of $\Gamma$ gives a nilpair
nodes.statement: By Lemma \ref{lem:gpequivcong}, if this action of $\Gamma$ defines a groupable congruence on $K\backslash G$ then  $(K,\Gamma)$ is a nilpair.

nodes.name: Fiber-transitivity of $\Gamma_\bullet$ on $K\backslash G$
nodes.statement: Let $(G,G_\bullet)$ be a filtered group of finite degree $k$. Let $K,\Gamma$ be subgroups of $G$. The following statements are equivalent: \begin{enumerate}[leftmargin=0.7cm] \item The filtration $\Gamma_\bullet:=(\Gamma\cap G_i)_{i\ge 0}$ is fiber-transitive on the coset nilspace $K\backslash G$. \item For any $x\in G$ and all $i\ge 0$ we have $(Kx\Gamma)\cap(KxG_i)=Kx(\Gamma\cap G_i)$. \end{enumerate}

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 7.3
nodes.statement: Let us recall a useful fact about coset nilspaces. If $(G,G_\bullet)$ is of degree $k$ and $K$ is a subgroup of $G$, the $(i-1)$-step nilspace factor of $K\backslash G$ is isomorphic to the coset nilspace associated with the filtered group $(G/G_i,(G_j/G_i)_{j\ge 0})$ and the subgroup $(K G_i)/G_i$. Assume now that $(ii)$ holds. Suppose that for some $\gamma\in \Gamma$, $x,y\in G$ we have $Kx\gamma=Ky$ and $\pi_{i-1}(Kx)=\pi_{i-1}(Ky)$. The last equality means that \[ (K G_i/G_i) (xG_i) = (K G_i/G_i) (y G_i). \] Hence, for some $s\in K$ we have $(sG_i)(xG_i)=yG_i$. As $G_i$ is normal, this means that $sxG_i = yG_i$, so there exists $g\in G_i$ such that $xsg=y$. Since also $Kx\gamma=Ky$, for some $s'\in K$ we have $s'x\gamma=y$. Hence $s'x\gamma=xsg$. By $(ii)$ there exists some $t\in (\Gamma\cap G_i)$ such that $Ky=Kxh=K x t$ and $(i)$ follows. The converse is similar. Assuming $(i)$, let us just prove the inclusion $(Kx \Gamma)\cap(KxG_i)\subset K x(\Gamma\cap G_i)$ (the opposite inclusion is clear). Let $k,k'\in K$, $\gamma\in \Gamma$, $g\in G_i$ and $x\in G$ be such that $kx\gamma = k'x g$. Then $Kx \gamma = Kx g$ and $\pi_{i-1}(Kx)=\pi_{i-1}(Kxg)$, so by $(i)$ there exists $t\in \Gamma\cap G_i$ such that $Kxt=Kxg$. Thus for some $k''\in K$ we have $k''xt = k'xg$ and therefore $k'xg\in K x (\Gamma\cap G_i)$, as required.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 7.4
nodes.statement: We prove the implication $(i)\Rightarrow (ii)$, the converse is proved similarly. Assuming that $(i)$ holds, it then suffices to prove for every $i\ge 0$ and $x\in G$ the inclusion $(Kx{\Gamma})\cap(KxG_i)\subset Kx({\Gamma}\cap G_i)$ (the opposite inclusion is clear). We argue by induction on the degree $k$. For $k=1$ all groups are abelian and the result is clear. For $i>k$ the result is trivial. First we prove the required inclusion for $i=k$. Suppose that $gxs = g'xh$ is an element of $(Kx{\Gamma})\cap (KxG_k)$ for some $g,g'\in K$, $x\in G$, $s\in {\Gamma}$ and $h\in G_k$. Then, as the elements of $G_k$ commute with every other element of $G$ we have that $g'^{-1}gxs=hx$. Applying $(i)$ we get that this equals $txs'$ for some $t\in K\cap G_k$ and $s'\in {\Gamma}$. Again, as the elements of $G_k$ commute with everything, we get that $ht^{-1}=s'\in {\Gamma}$ and by definition $ht^{-1}\in G_k$ as well. Hence $Kx({\Gamma}\cap G_k)\supset Kxht^{-1} = Kxh$ (again using that $t\in G_k$ commutes with everything). Now we prove the inclusion of any $i<k$ by induction on $k$. Let $gxs = g'xh$ be an element of $(Kx{\Gamma})\cap (KxG_i)$. Passing to the quotient $G/G_k$, note that on the filtered group $(G/G_k,(G_i/G_k)_{i\ge 0})$ we have the action of $KG_k/G_k$ on the left and of ${\Gamma}G_k/G_k$ on the right. Hence, by induction on $k$ we know that there exists $g''\in K$ and $t\in G_i\cap ({\Gamma}G_k)$ such that $gxsG_k = g'xhG_k=g''xtG_k$. We can write $t=s_tg_t$ for some elements $s_t\in {\Gamma}$ and $g_t\in G_k$. Thus, for some $z\in G_k$ we have that $gxss_t^{-1} =g'' xg_tz$. But $ss_t^{-1}\in {\Gamma}$ and $g_tz\in G_k$ so we can apply the case $i=k$ proved previously to conclude that for some $r\in {\Gamma}\cap G_k$ and $g'''\in K$ we have $gxss_t^{-1} =g'' xg_tz= g'''xr$. Hence $gxs = g''' x rs_t$, where $rs_t\in \Gamma$ and $rs_t = r s_tg_tg_t^{-1} = r tg_t^{-1}\in G_i$ as $r,g_t^{-1}\in G_k$ and $t\in G_i$, so $rs_t\in \Gamma\cap G_i$ as required.
